tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Galaxies & Galaxy Types

questions.question: Q: Name the three main types of galaxies.
questions.correctAnswer: Elliptical, spiral (including barred spiral), and irregular.

questions.question: Q: What does the Hubble tuning-fork diagram show?
questions.correctAnswer: It classifies galaxies by shape — ellipticals on the left (E0–E7), normal spirals on the upper branch (Sa–Sd), barred spirals on the lower branch (SBa–SBd). It is a classification, NOT an evolutionary sequence.

questions.question: Q: How do elliptical and spiral galaxies differ in content?
questions.correctAnswer: Elliptical galaxies contain mostly old red stars with little gas or dust and minimal star formation. Spiral galaxies contain a mix of old and young stars with gas and dust in the disc, allowing ongoing star formation.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Galaxies & Galaxy Types

questions.question: Q: What is the Local Group?
questions.correctAnswer: A gravitationally bound cluster of over 80 galaxies, including the Milky Way, Andromeda (M31) and the Triangulum Galaxy (M33).

questions.question: Q: What will happen when the Milky Way and Andromeda collide?
questions.correctAnswer: They are approaching each other at ~110 km/s and will merge in about 4.5 billion years, likely forming a large elliptical galaxy. Individual stars are unlikely to collide due to vast separations.
